title: The state of ICT in Mozambique - Research ICT Africa

facts.fact: Mozambique's telecommunications market is structured around four vertically-integrated operators, including fixed-line incumbent TDM.
facts.quote: The telecommunications market is structured around four vertically-integrated operators, including fixed-line incumbent, Telecomunicações de Moçambique (TDM).

facts.fact: Movitel, a joint venture between Viettel Group and SPI, launched as the third mobile player in Mozambique in 2011, ending the Vodacom Mozambique and mCel duopoly.
facts.quote: the launch of the third player Movitel, a joint venture between the Viettel Group of Vietnam and Mozambique’s SPI

facts.fact: In the After Access Survey 2017 across 16 Global South countries, Mozambique's mobile phone penetration was 30%.
facts.quote: Mozambique had among the lowest mobile phone and Internet penetration rates, 30% and 10%, respectively.

facts.fact: In the After Access Survey 2017 across 16 Global South countries, Mozambique's Internet penetration was 10%.
facts.quote: Mozambique had among the lowest mobile phone and Internet penetration rates, 30% and 10%, respectively.

facts.fact: Movitel's share of total mobile revenue rose to 27 percent in 2016, according to the page.
facts.quote: increasing its revenue share to 27 percent in 2016

facts.fact: Movitel's share of mobile revenue was about 11 percent in 2012, according to the page.
mCel held only 21 percent of total mobile revenue in 2016, according to the page.
facts.quote: leaving mCel with only 21 percent of the total mobile revenue

facts.fact: Vodacom Mozambique's data revenue grew 31 percent and its data customers grew 63.6 percent, per the page; the page notes this is off a very low base.
facts.quote: Vodacom’s data revenue grew by 31 percent and data customers increased by 63.6 percent

facts.fact: Vodacom Mozambique's data revenue reached MZN 3.7 million, according to the page.
Research ICT Africa ranks Mozambique third among 49 African countries on 1GB data pricing (RAMP data), above Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.
facts.quote: Among 49 African countries, Research ICT Africa ranks Mozambique third above Ghana, Kenya and South Africa.

facts.fact: Mozambique has the lowest mobile phone adoption level (50%) and the second highest gender disparity at 36 percent, after Rwanda's 38 percent.
facts.quote: Mozambique has the lowest mobile phone adoption level (50%) and the second highest gender disparity at 36 percent after Rwanda’s 38 percent.

facts.fact: Only 32 percent of women in Mozambique have mobile phones, according to the After Access Survey as cited on the page.
facts.quote: as compared to only 32 percent of women.

facts.fact: Of those offline in Mozambique (90%), 76 percent said they do not have devices to access the Internet.
facts.quote: Of those who are offline (90%), 76 percent stated that they do not have devices to access the Internet

facts.fact: 78 percent of respondents without a mobile phone in Mozambique said they cannot afford one.
facts.quote: 78 percent of the respondents stated that they cannot afford a mobile phone.

facts.fact: Mozambique's smartphone penetration is seven percent, which the page links to its ten percent Internet penetration.
facts.quote: Mozambique stands at seven percent, which explains the low ten percent, Internet penetration in Mozambique.

facts.fact: About two-thirds (64%) of respondents without smartphones said smartphones are too expensive.
facts.quote: about two-thirds (64%) stated that smartphones are too expensive

facts.fact: Half of the Mozambican population has no access to electricity, compared with six percent in South Africa and 33 percent in Nigeria.
facts.quote: Half of the Mozambican population has no access to electricity, compared to only six percent in South Africa and 33 percent in Nigeria.

facts.fact: 36% of those without mobile phones in Mozambique cited lack of electricity as the main reason.
facts.quote: A substantial proportion (36%) of those who do not have mobile phones reported lack of electricity
